name: unfairness
description: A perception that an outcome was not balanced as it should be.
perceptions: An outcome occurred where some people got more or less of something than they deserved.
examples: One person gets a bigger piece of pie.

guidance.description: What Should You Do When Life is Unfair? Dealing with Unfairness

variations.name: injustice
variations.description: A perception that the outcome or process of a social judgement was not aligned with deeply important rules.
perceptions: Someone chose an outcome that affects me.
I don't agree with the outcome.
They did not adhere to the moral rules as they should have.
examples: A false accusation wrongly lands someone in prison.
A good person has a bad thing happen to them.

comparisons.description: An injustice is a type of unfairness where there's a moral or legal aspect.

guidance.description: Persistent anger and feelings of injustice—directed toward a particular person, circumstance, or yourself—come with a steep price tag: They rob you of happiness in the moment and have negative impacts on your health. Here’s what you can do to begin to gain control so you have a better outcome. After all, you can't change what happened in the past. The only thing you can alter is your present experience.

variations.name: unfairness of nature
variations.description: A perception that the natural world is attacking people, animals, or plants.
perceptions: Nature is not always fair to people, animal, and plant individuals.

guidance.description: Since life is not a symphony of fairness, but a jazz improvisation of asymmetries, the first step towards acceptance  is to acknowledge this inherent randomness, this inherent unfairness. It is not an enemy to be defeated, but a dance partner to be embraced.

comparisons.description: Losing can feel unfair if you suspect someone cheated to win. But you may also recognize a loss as having been fair.

commentaries.quote: 'Fairness' can depend on context that's not always immediately visible. Maybe the kid who got the bigger piece of pie worked all day for it and the other kids did nothing.
He who commits injustice is ever made more wretched than he who suffers it.
The ultimate tragedy is not the oppression and cruelty by the bad people but the silence over that by the good people.
I always write about war, love, death, and injustice. There's plenty of that around, so I never run out of ideas.
If something seems unfair, just prove yourself by working twice as hard and being twice as good.

We're all glad that we aren’t bad people until we wake up one morning and say, 'What have I done?' Our brains are hard-wired toward self-serving bias. A whole slew of psychological biases facilitates our bad behavior, helping us justify, rationalize, selectively forget and attribute in ways that are self-serving.
Nature was neither fair nor unfair. Those terms belonged to the world of men.
